spec.description: Backend deployment performance metrics. Application metrics via :9090/actuator/prometheus (Spring Boot/WebFlux/r2dbc). Pod resource metrics from kubelet cAdvisor. Namespace and deployment filters are available in the top bar.
Time spent in GC per second (pause sum rate). Consistently >0.1 means CPU is going to GC
spec.title: GC overhead — by pod

spec.description: Eden/Survivor/Old Gen (heap) + Metaspace/CodeHeap (non-heap). Steady rise in Old Gen baseline after GC suggests a leak
spec.title: JVM memory breakdown (by pool, all pods combined)

spec.description: Netty/R2DBC off-heap usage. Visible in container working set but not in JVM heap
spec.title: Direct buffer memory — by pod

spec.description: End of minor/major GC — frequent major GC is a problem
spec.title: GC count (by action)

spec.description: High allocation rate → Eden pressure; high promotion rate + filling Old Gen → GC pressure
spec.title: Allocation / promotion rate (total)

spec.description: Heap surviving after Full GC. Steady growth is a classic memory leak signal
spec.title: Live data size (heap baseline after GC) — by pod

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (increase(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$deployment-.+", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (increase(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$deployment-.+", container!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description: Throttled CFS periods / total periods. Should be 0 on unlimited pods; >10% → increase limit
spec.title: CPU throttling — by pod

spec.description: HTTP request rate per pod; uneven load distribution across pods is visible here
spec.title: TPS — by pod

spec.description: Spring Boot HikariCP metrics. total = active + idle. Max line is maximum-pool-size (per pod). All pods combined.
spec.title: Hikari pool connections

spec.description: If pending > 0 persists, pool is bottlenecked (thread waiting for connection). Rising timeouts mean requests are dropped without a connection → increase max-size or find slow queries.
spec.title: Pending acquire + timeout

spec.description: Time to acquire a connection from the pool. avg = rate(sum)/rate(count). Rising value indicates pool saturation.
spec.title: Connection acquire time (pool wait)

spec.description: Time a connection is held. High values mean slow queries or long transactions are occupying connections.
spec.title: Connection usage time (connection hold duration)

spec.description: rate(sum) / rate(count). Histogram buckets not exposed, p95 cannot be calculated
spec.title: Average response time

spec.description: Spring Boot ConnectionPoolMetrics (r2dbc-pool). allocated = active + idle. Max line is pool max-size.
spec.title: Pool connections

spec.description: If >0 persists, pool is bottlenecked: increase max-size or investigate slow queries
spec.title: Pending acquire (requests waiting for a connection)

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$deployment-.+", container!=""}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$deployment-.+", container!=""})

spec.description: OOM kills are based on this. JVM heap + non-heap + direct buffer + native; always higher than micrometer heap is normal
spec.title: Container memory (working set) — by pod
